newsitem.title: FRANCE: Daughters row over Publicis stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daughters row over Publicis stake - paper.

text.p: Two daughters of Publicis founder Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet are embroiled in a row over one of them trying to sell her stake in the French advertising agency's holding company, financial daily La Tribune said on Monday.

It said Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, the Publicis founder's youngest daughter, is trying to sell the holdings she inherited on her father's death last year. This includes a one-third stake in Somarel, the Publicis holding company which in turn owns 38.4 percent of Publicis's capital and 45 percent of its voting rights.
She also owns over seven percent of Publicis directly. Altogether her share of Publicis, direct and indirect, is estimated at 20 percent, worth nearly a billion francs, La Tribune said.
It said Elisabeth Badinter, the founder's second daughter and chairman of Somarel, is using a complex legal structure to prevent her sister from selling her various stakes.
No one was immediately available at Publicis to comment.

The supervisory board of Publicis, which includes financiers Michel-David Weill of Banque Lazard and Edmond de Rothschild, has not been called in officially but is unofficially trying to resolve the row, it said.

The newspaper said 8.5 percent of Publicis which belonged to its founder still has to be shared out among those who inherit from him. The stock, with only 36 percent quoted on the Paris bourse, is much sought out by investors, it added.
